system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A successful network logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 as sam.okafor came from WS-LMARTINS-01. This is inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is performed only from WS-SOKAFOR-01.
DropboxUpdate.exe ran briefly as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01, although Dropbox/file-sharing services are not approved in the supplied environment context.
During the DropboxUpdate.exe execution, svchost.exe queried x7k9m2.akamaized.net, which resolved to 151.101.25.122. The logs do not establish that DropboxUpdate.exe caused the query.

The periodic HTTPS activity that triggered the alert is consistent with the approved PixelForge updater: pfupdater.exe connected through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.com at roughly five-minute intervals. One attempt received a proxy 407 response before later successful tunnels.
WS-LMARTINS-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-NWD-01 that resulted in an ANONYMOUS LOGON record. The available records do not show what resource or action was involved.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records provide CONNECT tunnel summaries, not the HTTPS paths, content, or downloaded update details; examples include T046-00101 and T046-00219.

The DNS query for x7k9m2.akamaized.net is logged under svchost.exe, and the available records do not link it to DropboxUpdate.exe or show a subsequent connection to the resolved address (T046-00119, T046-00124, T046-00126).
The successful logon record identifies the source and target account/host but does not show what actions, if any, followed on WS-SOKAFOR-01 (T046-00024).
The records show a short-lived DropboxUpdate.exe process but do not establish whether Dropbox was installed or used for file transfer, or whether that binary was authorized (T046-00119, T046-00127).
claims_not_established: Whether sam.okafor's credentials were used with authorization or were compromised.
Whether the logon to WS-SOKAFOR-01 led to remote administration, access to data, or changes on that host.
Whether DropboxUpdate.exe made an outbound connection or transferred any data.
Whether the periodic PixelForge update responses contained legitimate software or were tampered with.
What activity occurred over the SMB session to FILE-NWD-01.
additional_evidence_needed: Review WS-SOKAFOR-01 authentication, process, PowerShell, and remote-management logs around 13:26 UTC to determine what followed the sam.okafor logon.
Verify with sam.okafor whether the authentication from WS-LMARTINS-01 was authorized; review credential-use and endpoint records for possible exposure.
Collect DropboxUpdate.exe file hash, signature, installation/service details, and endpoint network telemetry around 13:42 UTC; correlate the DNS query and any proxy or direct connections.
Review FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and file-operation auditing for the WS-LMARTINS-01 session.
Validate the PixelForge updater binary and update package, and retrieve available proxy or endpoint TLS inspection details for the periodic connections.
